items.stem: If an electric current flows through a wire, and the wire is placed near a magnetic compass, what will happen to the compass needle?
What does the deflection of the compass needle indicate when current flows through a wire?
When an electric current flows through a wire, what happens to a magnetic compass placed near the wire?
What is the main purpose of using a magnetic compass in the experiment described in the passage?
What is the function of the iron nail in the electromagnet experiment described in the passage?
What happens to the magnetic field around a wire when the electric current through it is stopped?

An electromagnet is made by winding a coil of insulated wire around an iron nail and connecting it to a cell. When the cell is connected, the nail becomes a magnet and attracts iron paper clips. What happens to the magnetic strength of the electromagnet if the number of turns in the coil is increased?

A student places a magnetic compass near the two ends of an electromagnet. When the current is turned on, the compass needle deflects. The student observes that the compass needle is attracted to end A of the electromagnet. What can be concluded about the polarity of end A?
Which of the following is an example of an appliance that works on the heating effect of electric current?

An electromagnet is made by winding a coil of 10 turns around an iron nail and connecting it to a cell. A second electromagnet is made by winding 20 turns around the same iron nail and connecting it to the same cell. Which of the two electromagnets will have a stronger magnetic field?

In an experiment, a student uses a coil of 20 turns to make an electromagnet. He then replaces the coil with one of 40 turns, keeping the same cell and iron nail. What change would he observe in the magnetic strength of the electromagnet?
What does the passage suggest about the heat generated in a wire?

A student performs an experiment to observe the heating effect of electric current in a wire. They use a battery with 2 cells and notice that the wire heats up. What would happen if they use a battery with 1 cell instead?
What is the purpose of using appropriate wires, plugs, and sockets in household circuits, according to the passage?
Which of the following best explains why the chemicals in a Voltaic cell eventually get used up?
In which of the following cases will the compass needle deflect when current flows through the coil?
When electric current flows through a conductor, which of the following effects is produced?
In which of the following cases will the magnetic compass needle definitely show deflection?
If the temperature of a copper wire increases while it is connected in a circuit, what happens to its electrical resistance?
Why is nichrome wire commonly used in electric heating devices?
Which of the following is an example of the magnetic effect of electric current?
An electric room heater is used for a long time, and the wire becomes very hot. What would happen if the same heater was used with a thicker wire?
In an experiment, a copper wire was connected to a battery with two cells, and it heated up. What would happen if the battery was replaced with a single cell?
Which of the following factors does NOT affect the heat generated in a wire due to electric current?
In a science experiment, a student used a lemon cell with copper and iron electrodes to light an LED. The LED did not glow at first. What could be the reason?
Which of the following is NOT a heating appliance mentioned in the passage?
In an experiment, a coil of wire is connected to a cell and placed near a magnetic compass. When current is passed through the coil, the compass needle deflects. What causes this deflection?

An electromagnet is made by winding a coil of wire around an iron nail. When the current is passed through the coil, the nail attracts iron clips. What happens to the magnetic effect of the nail when the current is stopped?
In an experiment, two identical coils are used. One coil has 100 turns and the other has 200 turns. Both are connected to the same battery. Which coil will produce a stronger magnetic field?
What is the name of the phenomenon when a current carrying wire produces a magnetic field around it?
In the experiment described, what happens to the iron paper clips when the current stops flowing through the coil?
Which of the following is a property of an electromagnet?
What happens to a nichrome wire when electric current flows through it?
Which of the following is a correct statement about rechargeable batteries?
What is the main reason why an electromagnet becomes a magnet when current is passed through it?
If the temperature of a copper wire increases while it is in a circuit, what happens to its resistance?
